narrative.overview: The window is a piece of hardware with rounded corners. The chrome (title bar, front panel, toolbar, status bar) is one sheet of brushed scarlet aluminium with white legends. Set into it on the left is a black OLED window that spans the full width of the 61-key keyboard and holds everything you read: a status line, the grand staff, the chord name, the circle of fifths and the chord strip. Below the OLED window and practice toolbar, behind a felt strip, sit real white and black keys. In the right-hand hardware column beside the OLED display and keys sit two halo knobs for volume and click, twelve rubber panel keys with LEDs, and the vector HØJT hardware badge.
keyCharacteristics: One scarlet panel, brushed, shared by every chrome surface without seams on a 14px hardware grid.
One black OLED window with a bezel spans the full width of the 61-key keyboard and holds the readout and diatonic chord strip.
Real keys, neutral white with no ivory yellowing: a held key goes down and lights blue along its back edge, and out-of-key keys dim when a key signature is active.
A right-hand hardware front panel of rotary halo knobs, twelve LED rubber keys, and the HØJT hardware badge.
On means white: a lit toggle, the primary action, and the played chord tile are white with black ink.

rules.name: The One Panel Rule
rules.body: Every chrome surface is the same brushed scarlet. Separation inside the chrome comes from black rubber controls and legends, never from a second red.

rules.name: The Window Holds the Reading Rule
rules.body: Whatever you read mid-phrase (chord, numeral, notes, staff, circle, chord strip) sits in the black OLED window. The panel carries controls and labels only.

rules.name: The On Means White Rule
rules.body: A switched-on toggle, the one primary action and the played chord tile are white keys with black ink. Amber never means 'on'; blue never means 'on'.

rules.name: The One Job Per Hue Rule
rules.body: Amber is what waits on you; blue is you playing; magenta is the app asking; teal and violet are your hands; green is hit; red is miss and recording.

rules.name: The Data Holds Still Rule
rules.body: Monospace is for pitches, intervals, levels, the MIDI log and clocks, so digits don't shift as they change.

rules.name: The Set-In Rule
rules.body: A surface either sits in the panel (the OLED window, the knob recesses) or is a black key on it. There are no shadows on panels, tiles or inputs.

dos: **Do** build every brush from a `Color.*` token in `Dark.xaml` and resolve it by key in code-behind renderers.
**Do** put anything read mid-phrase inside the OLED window, and controls and legends on the panel.
**Do** mark 'on' and the single primary action with a white key and Ink.
**Do** give disabled controls the Disabled Fill, never the panel brush.
**Do** keep words at Legend Muted or brighter on the scarlet; Legend Faint draws marks only.
donts: **Don't** add a second red to the chrome, or a gradient across the panel that makes tiles band.
**Don't** use amber as decoration or to mean 'on'.
**Don't** borrow blue for selection or 'on'; blue means you are playing.
**Don't** use the halos' green-to-red scale anywhere but the halos.
**Don't** use Unicode look-alike glyphs (✕, ↻, □) for icons; use Segoe MDL2 Assets codes or a drawn path.
